A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same active-learning benchmarking project despite the changed title and expanded scope. All 41 pages of v2 and 47 pages of v3, including appendices, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark runs on 26 binary datasets, model-compatibility experiments, and statistical analyses, including Tables 1 and 3 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 reports original XGBoost and Random Forest benchmarks, multiclass and domain-specific evaluations, and sensitivity experiments, alongside retained reproduction results.

M1.justification: The query, label, pool-update, and retraining framework and separation of query-oriented and task-oriented models remain unchanged. The added learners, feature representations, and batch-size trials extend the evaluation; the PDFs do not establish a revision to a proposed learning algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 retains the 26 binary datasets and evaluates four additional binary datasets, eight multiclass datasets, and CIFAR-10 and IMDB representations (Table 17). Myocardial and RT-IoT2022 participate in the imbalanced one-shot study. This substantially expands task, domain, scale, and population coverage beyond v2.

E2.justification: The primary comparison suite changes from 17 strategies to 12 representatives plus newly evaluated BALD. EER, VR, SPAL, US-NC, and InfoDiv are omitted from the new tree-model suite, while distinct multiclass US measures are compared in Table 8. The original RBF-SVM comparator suite and BSO remain in Appendix C.

E3.justification: v3 adds full XGBoost/RF comparisons, a 3000-query budget cap for large datasets, and budget-specific accuracy, stopping-point, data-utilization, and weighted-F1 evaluations. The stated execution limit changes from 1080 to 72 hours. New protocols include one-shot initialization and batch-size variation. Whether the main initial sets are fixed is inconsistently described between Section 3 and Appendix C.3.

E4.justification: Beyond retained compatibility and dataset-property analyses, v3 adds Checkerboard/Banana failure investigations (Figures 5–7), default-versus-tuned XGBoost sensitivity (Figure 11), batch-size tests (Table 11), and fixed-versus-random initial-set analysis (Table 24). The imbalanced one-shot study also examines an additional failure condition.

E5.justification: v2's paired-t-test usefulness summary is removed. v3 introduces highlighting based on exceeding Uniform's mean plus one standard deviation in Tables 8–10, a different comparison rule. Reporting of 100/10 runs, Friedman ranking tests, and t-based reproduction comparisons is retained; an increase in repeated-run counts is not established.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive model, multiclass, domain-specific, efficiency, sensitivity, and timing results. Table 3 reports US leading on 18/29 binary datasets, and Table 8 reports US-SM leading on 5/7 multiclass datasets under the new settings. New RBF-SVM Table 19 also contains values differing from the retained v2 results in Table 20, such as Sonar Uniform at 75.00% versus 74.63%; these differences cannot be interpreted as established same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The BMDR objective, binary uncertainty-measure equivalence argument, and applicability-score definitions are retained. However, v2 Appendix D.1's quadratic subproblem and eigenvalue-shift argument for kernel stabilization are removed. This is a limited removal of mathematical reasoning; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion reposition the work from correcting binary-classification benchmarks to providing a comprehensive survey and benchmark supporting practical recommendations across models and classification tasks. The US/model-compatibility claim remains, while v2's finding that over half the strategies lack significant advantages over Uniform is no longer a principal contribution.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations involving unexplored regions and sampling bias, model complexity under tuning, and redundancy in batch querying. It also develops limitations for imbalanced one-shot learning and domain-specific representations. Section 4.3.2 explicitly discusses external knowledge from pretraining and missing comparisons with alternative representation-learning protocols, substantially qualifying applicability.

D1.justification: v3 adds pretrained ViT/BERT identifiers, model-choice documentation, and an in-paper timing table where v2 provided an online-results link. Conversely, v2 Appendix D's CVXPY error trace, kernel regularization, psd_wrap, and OSQP troubleshooting details are removed. Hardware and the main code-repository disclosure remain; removal of documentation does not establish reversal of those implementation fixes.

R1.justification: The four-category review becomes a six-category survey with substantial discussion of Bayesian methods and modern tabular, transformer, cross-domain, and foundation-model research. Added works include Houlsby et al., Bahri et al., Grinsztajn et al., Rauch et al., Werner et al., and Gupte et al. The contribution is positioned more broadly as a practical survey and expanded benchmark.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Section 2 becomes an expanded literature survey, the original reproduction narrative moves largely to Appendices B–C, and new benchmark and analysis sections organize the main text. These changes substantially restructure the narrative beyond simply inserting new experiments.

P2.justification: v3 adopts the wider TMLR layout and substantially redesigns tables, including dense strategy comparisons and color-marked data-utilization tables. It adds strategy illustrations, failure-case panels, sensitivity plots, and timing displays. Earlier results are relocated, the significance-count figure is removed, and different retained compatibility heatmaps are selected for the main text.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the practical basis of the US recommendation through broader model/task evaluation, direct labeling-efficiency measures, and evidence about sensitivity and failure conditions. These address important applicability gaps in v2's predominantly binary RBF-SVM benchmark. Conflicting initialization descriptions and RBF-SVM tables, together with deleted solver troubleshooting, weaken reproducibility clarity, but the broader and more carefully qualified empirical evidence provides a substantial net improvement.
